meta.title: Global Groove
meta.author: WaveSabre Team (the song's own composer is not named in the repository)
meta.description: Global Groove, a Renoise project in the WaveSabre converter test suite that exercises the Global Groove parameters. This is an adapted version, not the original recording: The project was converted to a WaveSabre song (the `synth-mix` layout), then by `synth-convert ws` to the unified synth (instrument kind 64, effects kinds 65-73), then imported with `song import` (lanes cut into 2-, 4- or 8-bar patterns with variants, notes rounded to 960 ticks per beat; track names from the original project where it has them). Instruments and effects are the unified equivalents of the WaveSabre devices and sound close to, not identical with, the original (parity target: 1 dB loudness, 3 dB per octave band).

about.style: tiny 4-bar Renoise test project that exercises Renoise's Global Groove (swing) setting; a single noise tick, not a piece of music
about.description: Four bars of one repeated noise click on a 16th-note grid, routed through one bus to the master. It exists to check that the converter reproduces Renoise's Global Groove timing, so it has no arrangement, melody or key.

about.engine: WaveSabre Slaughter: all three oscillators muted, noise at full level, filter open, zero decay and sustain with a very short release
about.description: Repeats one note (C3, full velocity) on the 16th grid across all 4 bars as a timing probe for the groove/swing setting. It sounds like a dry, closed-hat-like tick.

about.engine: Renoise track used as a bus; no WaveSabre devices
about.description: Receives the Slaughter track and passes it on to the master without processing.
